summary: A 73-foot steel observatory on Peters Mountain in McCreary County, ready to be manned in April 1938; its later fate is not in the sources found.

Six residents of Stearns convicted of damaging the tower; sentences suspended, probation, and payment to the Forest Service for the damage

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1938 report names the Cumberland National Forest; the NHLR entry for the Stearns tower says that forest was later renamed the Daniel Boone National Forest.

sources.title: Datasheet listing for NGS station GB2629 (Peters Mountain Lot)

notes_for_editor: No source says whether the tower still stands, and access is unknown. Heights disagree and are unexplained: 73 ft in the 1938 report (kept here as 22.3 m) versus 90 ft in the 1950 Coast and Geodetic Survey description. The NGS listing for GB2629 has two rows (codes XX and NN); only the surface-mark code is quoted, and it concerns the survey mark, not the tower. The history rests on one compiled page of newspaper excerpts (Lexington Herald-Leader 13 Dec 1937, Kentucky Advocate 7 Apr 1938, Lexington Leader 7 Nov 1970); the originals are worth checking if someone has newspaper access. The Daniel Boone National Forest may know the current status. The link between the 1950 survey point and GB2629 comes from the lookout page (its designation line), not from the NGS listing, which carries only the name. The second NGS row (code NN, no geodetic control) is not in the story.
